To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) SRB are able to survive in particle-free drinking water and mineral medium under oligotrophic and oxygen stress conditions; (ii) the culturability of SRB in drinking and mineral medium decreases faster than the metabolic activity of the cells; and (iii), the coculture with A. commune prolongs the culturability and the metabolic activity of SRB.

the behavior of SRB under oxygen stress and oligotrophic conditions depends on the strain, and that the response to oxygen stress and oligo- or starvation conditions can be influenced by the presence of aerobic microorganisms.
the behavior of sulfate reducing bacteria is strain dependent and that the presence of other organisms may influence the behavior of sulfate reducers in coculture experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the in situ identification and quantification of SRB in particle-free systems.
the behavior of SRB under oligotrophic and oxygen stress conditions in particle-free drinking water and mineral medium.
the behavior of SRB under oxygen stress and carbon depletion conditions in particle-free drinking water.

the response of SRB to carbon starvation and oxygen stress is strain specific, which is also reflected by the results obtained in pure culture tests and coculture experiments with A. commune.
the response of SRB towards oxygen stress and carbon deprivation is strain specific.

the environmental strains zt3 and zt10 are more stress-resistant than the type strains of the species D. baculatu and D. desulfuricans, respectively, and that the coculture with A. commune is a promising approach to study the response of SRB to stress.

the behavior of SRB under oligotrophic and oxygen stress conditions is strain dependent, and that the presence of aerobic bacteria in the coculture tests may have a protective effect on SRB.

the behavior of SRB under oligotrophic and oxygen stress conditions depends on the strain and the environmental conditions.
